newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: U.S. film, TV force News profit up sharply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. film, TV force News profit up sharply.

text.p: News Corp's Fox Television and Fox Films, driven by the success of the Star Wars series, were the driving force in a 34 percent rise in News' profit before abnormals to A$376 million in the three months to March 31, News Corp said on Thursday.
British newspapers and BSkyB also produced significant profit contributions, News said.
News' book publishing and Australasian newspaper and pay television were the main drags on profit, it said.
Net profit after abnormals rose to A$330 million from A$77 million a year earlier.
There was an abnormal loss of A$46 million for the quarter, compared with a A$204 million loss in the previous comparable quarter.
"These results reflect strong double digit earnings increases at all of the company's core operating sgements with the exception of Book Publishing," News said.
"Particularly strong gains were recorded in the U.S. Television Group, Filmed Entertainment, FSI (Free Standing Inserts) and U.K. newspaper segments," it said.
"HarperCollins' results were off against last year reflecting weaker U.S. industry trends."
The abnormal loss related to the end of the CD-ROM publishing divisions at HarperCollins and News International and a restructuring at one of HarperCollins' U.S. division.
News said operating income from its Filmed Entertainment division, which includes Fox Films, rose to A$82 million from A$63 million in the same period a year earlier.
Filmed Entertainment revenues rose to A$1.138 billion from A$584 million.
News said Filmed Entertainment was bolstered by the box office performance of Star Wars Special Edition and its two sequels.
"Since being released at the end of January Star Wars has generated US$138 million at the domestic box office, with the two sequels adding another US$111 million to date," News said.
U.S. television operating income rose to A$135 million from A$77 million, with revenues rising to US$959 million from US$820 million.
"Softness in national and retail display advertising related to the slowing economy has hampered any meaningful revenue growth," News Corp said of the Australia newspaper unit.

It said the Foxtel pay-tv joint venture in Australia with the Telstra Corp telecoms unit of the national government had experienced a strong lift in subscriber orders since the Australian Super League rugby league competition began on February 28.
Foxtel now passes more than 1.6 million homes with current subscribers of more than 175,000 with a further 21,000 awaiting connection.
